title: Calibrate chart smoothing and attribution for late-ingest usage events
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem statement: Console charts (per-model breakdowns and per-tenant usage) show large, temporally-incorrect spikes when ingestion pipelines backfill or when delayed events arrive. This impacts billing visibility and causes customers and SRE to open false incident reports. Root causes appear to be a combination of the timeseries materialized rollup windows applying events to the "arrival_time" instead of the event's "ingest_time", plus frontend chart smoothing that unintentionally amplifies short-duration backfilled bursts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console per-model line charts display usage with deterministic attribution for delayed events: backfilled events are visually marked and optionally hidden via toggle. 2) Aggregation logic attributes tokens to event.ingest_time bucket and preserves original event_time for audit. 3) Nightly reconciliation job reconciles raw events with rollups and corrects discrepancies >0.5% for any 24h window. 4) New alert if ingestion_lag > 3 hours for any customer/partition. 5) UX toggle added: "Show backfilled data" default off for last 48h, with tooltip explaining re-attribution.
implementation_notes:
Planned changes:
- Ingestion/ETL: add explicit timestamp fields in event schema: event_time, ingest_time, source_time. Ensure CDC/pipeline preserves event_time on replay/backfill. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/243)
- Aggregator: change materialized view queries to bucket by ingest_time when calculating per-window billing metrics; keep event_time in raw_event table for audit. Modify retention and compaction to support late-arrival correction windows (grace period: 72h).
- Reconciliation job: implement nightly job (Python Spark/Beam) that scans raw_event vs rollup deltas and emits correction patches. Store patch audit log in billing_corrections table and surface in Console.
- Console: add smoothing calibration—switch from exponential smoothing that uses future lookahead to a causal moving average for last-24h windows. Add visual indicator for corrected/backfilled points and a toggle to hide/show. Update Chart service to request "include_backfill=true/false" parameter.
- Telemetry: emit metrics: ingestion_lag_histogram, corrected_tokens_count, rollup_discrepancy_rate. Add Grafana dashboard and PagerDuty rule for ingestion_lag > 3h sustained 15m.

Trade-offs considered:
- Applying corrections eagerly vs nightly: eager corrections reduce customer confusion but increase pipeline complexity and write amplification. We chose nightly reconciliation for initial rollout with a planned near-real-time short window in Q2 if stable.
- UX default hides backfilled data for short windows to avoid noisy spikes; power users can enable full view.
testing_plan: Unit tests for SQL rollup queries, integration tests with synthetic delayed events (various lag distributions), end-to-end test deploying reconciliation job to staging with shadowing, visual smoke tests comparing previous vs corrected chart outputs. Manual QA: reproduce a 6-hour backfill in staging and validate chart toggle and audit log. Performance test: ensure reconciliation job completes within maintenance window and rollup update queries don't exceed RCU limits.
comments: 2026-02-11 | Diego Marquez: Initial spike reproduction steps added. Reproduced on staging by replaying a batch of 4M token events with synthetic ingest_time 12h in the past. Observed that frontend smoothing amplified a 30-minute backfill into a 3-hour-looking spike.
2026-02-14 | Priya Nair (PM): Confirmed customer impact: 3 support tickets in Feb from two enterprise customers misreading billing spikes. Prioritizing as P1 for this cycle.

2026-02-18 | Diego Marquez: Prototype SQL change submitted. Key change: rollup_materialized_view now SELECT SUM(tokens) AS tokens_bucket, bucket_start FROM rollups GROUP BY bucket_start USING ingest_time_bucket(ingest_time, '1h', 3600). See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics/pull/509

2026-02-21 | SRE (Hannah Li): Noted edge case: Kafka partition rebalances produced duplicate replayed events; added dedupe hint to reconciliation job and idempotency key guidance to ingestion producers.
